title: test-inference-domain-stops-at-the-first-raise-and-prints-no-teeth-behind-it
author: CC
owner: CC builds it; cairn/devices/inference_domain owns the proof
intention: cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_inference_domain.py::_main() runs its checks in a loop that lets the first exception propagate, so every tooth behind the first red prints nothing at all. Give it the per-tooth shape its sibling already carries: catch per tooth, print 'FAIL <name>: <type>: <msg>', run the rest, and return non-zero with the red names listed.
why: Law 7 at a diagnostic surface. The readers of this proof's stdout are the hollow verb's teeth_printed and a human reading a failure — and for both, 'this tooth failed' and 'this tooth never ran' are opposite findings that send you to opposite work. The measured version of exactly this bug is already recorded in the sibling file's docstring: with the probe reverted away, the stop-at-first shape reported '1 proof(s) printed no teeth at all', and the hollow reading of that file was meaningless until the shape was fixed. This file has 20 teeth and is named by the same ticket's hollow runs; it is one revert away from the same silence.
how: Copy the shape from cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_the_agent_retry_probe_judges.py::main() (lines 162-185) — it exists, it is proven, and it was written against this exact measured failure. Per tooth: try/except BaseException, append the name to `red`, print the FAIL line; else print ok. Return 1 with the joined names when red is non-empty. Do not change what any tooth asserts.
falsifier: DONE when a deliberately-broken first tooth in test_inference_domain.py still leaves the other teeth printed by name, the FAIL line names the broken one, and the exit code is non-zero. WRONG INTENT if the teeth are reordered, split into separate files, or made to swallow their own assertions to keep the run green — the point is that a red is LEGIBLE, never that it is rarer.
traces_to: Law 7 (errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces; a surface that prints nothing for a tooth collapses failed into never-ran); Law 8 (the hollow reading depends on teeth being printed to attribute coverage to a file).
watchme: none, because the fix's own falsifier — break a tooth, see the others still print — is a deterministic check that lives in the proof file and runs on every seal.
gates_bound: proof gate — test_inference_domain.py runs green under the tester at isolation=netns, and the repaired runner prints every tooth with one deliberately broken.
feeds back to origin on failure — a red routes to this ticket's own voyage, never to a paragraph.
durability gate — not done until proven AND committed.
children: none, because it is one runner function in one file

decisions.text: Re-pointed 2026-10-18 from 'cairn/devices/inference_domain/intention+why.json' to cairn/tools/proof_coverage/intention+why.json. The answer to open-4122fee9293a ('the gate stays hard') puts the per-tooth runner in cairn/tools/proof_coverage/proof_coverage.py, the one file hollow reverts, so the crossing journals there. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-12 'approved thru PROVED, fastest route'

The build is run_teeth(checks) in cairn/tools/proof_coverage/proof_coverage.py, after print_teeth_main. It runs every check, prints '  ok    <name>' or '  FAIL  <name>: <type>: <msg>', and returns 1 when any is red. Its summary opens on a count ('<n> of <m> teeth red — <names>'), because 'red: ...' is the colon form _MARKER_LABEL reads as a red tooth (measured 2026-10-18 by the proof). It is NOT re-exported from __init__.py: the live proof_binds_its_subject_at_call_time sieve reds a module-level binding of a name the build added (measured 2026-10-18 on test_call_time_binding.py). test_inference_domain._main imports it from the module inside _main and calls it in place of the stop-at-first loop; no tooth there changes what it asserts. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-12 'approved thru PROVED, fastest route'

The proof is cairn/tools/proof_coverage/proofs/test_every_tooth_runs_and_a_red_is_named.py. Its tooth test_a_broken_first_tooth_leaves_the_rest_named covers the whole falsifier (clause 'all'): a broken first check is read red by name, the checks behind it are read green by name, the FAIL line carries the raise, and the exit is non-zero. Guards: an all-green run returns 0, and a non-assertion crash is a red. It resolves run_teeth at call time. Measured 2026-10-18: 3 of 3 red against today's code, 3 of 3 green with the change. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-12 'approved thru PROVED, fastest route'
